10.text: Chip stocks sold off sharply on Oct. 22 after Lam Research warned of supply chain constraints, with AMD and Marvell falling 8% and the semiconductor index dropping 6.7%. Stocks rebounded later in the week ahead of the Fed decision.

9.text: AMD shares rose 2.95% to $532.05 after a 137–156% yearly run and a 13% weekly drop, with earnings due November 3. Articles debate whether AI hyperscaler deals and a bullish CFO update justify the stock's 199x trailing earnings multiple.

12.text: Nvidia remains dominant in AI infrastructure, with CEO Jensen Huang reaffirming $3–4 trillion in annual data center capex by 2030, and its stock trading at an 11% discount to the S&P 500 despite expected profit growth. Anthropic's IPO filing shows up to $206 billion in computing contracts, but most are rentals and much goes to Google chips, bearing on AMD only as competitive context.

7.text: AMD expanded its Meta partnership to deploy Helios rackscale solutions and EPYC processors, with AMD investing $1B in Meta's equity offering tied to Meta's $95B AI infrastructure raise. AMD also landed Helios-based AI infrastructure deals in Europe and India, while Dell, Lenovo, Cisco, HPE, and Supermicro signed onto its Helios blueprint.

11.text: Tech stocks sold off sharply, with the Nasdaq down 2.6% and AMD falling alongside Nvidia, Meta, and Tesla amid AI-valuation concerns and Middle East tensions. Markets wobbled Friday as sentiment hit "Extreme Fear," though AMD is only mentioned in passing.

8.text: Marvell reported Q2 revenue of $2.74 billion, up 36.5% year-over-year on AI infrastructure demand, and its COO said supply and demand support $20 billion in revenue next year. Broadcom, not AMD, is framed as Nvidia's main custom-AI-chip threat, while AMD appears only in a four-stock portfolio piece.

17.text: Meta raised a $97.5 billion equity offering, upsized from roughly $35 billion, to fund AI infrastructure projected at $135–145 billion in 2026, with up to $60 billion more possible via an ATM program. The articles mention AMD only insofar as Meta's spending could benefit AI chip suppliers.

13.text: AMD and Broadcom both have strong medium-term AI chip outlooks, but the article picks one as more reasonably valued now. It's an investor comparison rather than new AMD developments.
